title.narrative: Civil society monitoring of the Ogoniland clean-up

description.narrative: The project will strengthen the ability of civil society to hold the Federal Government of Nigeria to account for a major clean-up of oil spills in the Niger Delta, focusing on the Ogoniland clean-up resulting from more than fifty years of oil spills in the region. It will do this by running an independent monitoring initiative to scrutinise the progress of the clean-up and make this information more accessible to the public.The track record of oil spill clean-ups in Nigeria in general is poor, and so ensuring the Ogoniland clean-up proceeds according to agreed standards – and documenting this if it does not take place – is vital to ensure the remediation of decades of damage to human and environmental health. Doing so will also help rebuild trust in government to protect Nigerians from the negative impact of the oil industry. This is a major obstacle to long to peace and social development in the Niger Delta, which has seen decades of conflict and instability.

"Key target groups include: ● Local communities, civil society organisations and their staff working on pollution-related issues in Ogoniland. In particular, this will include around 21 community members and at least 10 staff who will be trained as environmental monitors to take part in the project. They will have improved knowledge and capacity to implement technical environmental assessments, as well as increased links and trust with HYPREP officials and local impacted communities. This will lay the groundwork for further support to the long-term restoration of Ogoniland. ● 6 NOSDRA staff who will benefit from the same environmental monitoring training as civil society organisations. The project will also therefore build the capacity of relevant Nigerian regulators to carry out their mandate. ● Approximately 6 HYPREP staff, who will have improved understanding of the effectiveness of their work, and the opportunity to discuss the challenges with the clean-up in a constructive forum with civil society. This is significant, given the lack of confidence among all parties in Ogoniland, and may help ‘reset’ relations in a way that would support long term stability and development in the region. Beneficiaries will include: ● Approximately 850,000 people across Ogoniland, who will be able to have confidence that work to clean up their communities is being properly monitored. This in turn should lead to proper restoration of their land and water sources.

comment.narrative: Carry out interviews and surveys of stakeholders

1. CSOs during the stakeholder engagement in 2021, charged HYPREP to improve on their community relationship strategies to reduce conflict.2. CSOs during HYPREP's stakeholder engagement in 2022, asked HYPREP to work with all stakeholders to standardize TPH threshold values for the close-out of remediated lots.3. SDN released a press statement on Bloomberg in 2022 flagging possible shortfalls in the cleanup process, particularly in the local laboratory analyses of soil samples from clean-up lots and also recommending UNEP's continued provision of technical support to HYPREP to ensure best practice in the cleanup exercise.4. SDN-led CSOs, in 2022, decided to, and hence carried out, revegetation monitoring visits to already remediated/closed-out sites to ensure that the sites are satisfactorily restored to their default vegetative and agricultural use. Sites with poor revegetation have been identified, and will be flagged and reported to during advocacy engagements in 2023 for the needful corrective actions. 20235. SDN recommended the continued and more involvement of UNEP in the clean-up exercise. This was done during a meeting hosted by the UNEP at HYPREP office on the 16th of February, 2023.6. SDN urged phase 2 contractors of the Ogoni clean-up exercise to ensure proper engagement of communities and respectful management of the relationship between them and their host communities to ensure uninterrupted clean-up exercise.7. 42 environment monitors and CSOs received capacity enhancement on environmental monitoring methodologies to improve their ability to monitor the Ogoni clean-up exercise and hold HYPREP to account.8. CSOs discovered that revegetation in the certified clean-up lots is poor and noted it for discussion with HYPREP during the next stakeholders meeting so that the quality of remediation work should be improved upon.9. SDN charged potable water contractors to look into the quality of the potable water to ensure that meets the standard.10. SDN recommended that HYPREP should take note of potable water contractors that have been slow in their work and should examine them carefully before considering them for more potable water contracts.11. SDN expressed concerns about contractors owing community workers their allowances. This was made during the kick-off of the Batch 2 water projects.12. During the kick-off of the Batch 2 water projects SDN expressed concerns over gender inequality in engaging the community labour force and recommended more women inclusion.13. SDN expressed displeasure in the duration of the water projects were long overdue, and advocated for speedy completion so that the Ogoni people can have access to potable water as recommended by UNEP.14. SDN secured a working relationship on the clean-up of the entire Niger Delta and related issues with the appropriate Division in the Federal Ministry of Environment (Marine Protection, Contaminated Sites Clean-up and Remediation (MCCR) Division).15. CSOs recommended that HYPREP should review and improve their channels of communication for proper information dissemination.16. SDN recommended that HYPREP should involve communities during their evaluations so as to promote accuracy.17. CSOs recommended that HYPREP should step up their awareness strategy by including the use of local languages in Ogoniland.18. CSOs and community members recommended that HYPREP livelihood training beneficiaries should be named publicly in the communities so that the beneficiaries will be known.19. CSOs recommended that people with disabilities should be included in HYPREP engagement initiatives.20. During project review meetings organised by HYPREP, SDN-led CSOs recommended that biocells should be roofed, in line with the commitment made by HYPREP during the tenure of the farmer PC, Dr Ferdinand Giadom.21. SDN charged HYPREP Phase 2 remediation contractors to ensure that mistakes made in the Phase 1 clean-up are not repeated but corrected so that the exercise is implemented in line with UNEP’s recommendation.In response to SDN monitoring initiatives on the Ogoni clean-up, the following actions were taken by HYPREP:22. CSOs charged HYPREP to ensure closer monitoring of phase 2 contractors to ensure that the mistakes of phase 2 remediation are not repeated.23. CSOs engaged HYPREP and demanded that HYPREP should convert badly remediated and now damaged sites to infrastructural sites since the sites cannot support vegetation in the near future as a result of poor quality of work by Phase 1 contractors.24. CSOs engaged HYPREP and demanded that HYPREP should increase monitoring and evaluation of its livelihood programs to ensure success.25. CSOs engaged HYPREP and demanded that the growing cases of re-pollution at remediation sites and remediated sites should be urgently addressed.26. CSO and community heads engaged and demanded that HYPREP should employ more technical staff to enhance close technical monitoring of SMR sites remediation to ensure compliance with established guidelines.27. CSOs demanded that HYPREP should involve experts in the execution of livelihood programs to avoid delays and poorly executed livelihood programs.28. CSOs advocated that HYPREP should involve people with disabilities in the planning and execution of their projects to promote social inclusion.2024In response to SDN monitoring initiatives on the Ogoni clean-up, the following actions were taken by CSO to HYPREP:29. SDN-led CSOs demanded that contractors should be closely monitored during remedial action to ensure strict compliance with the requirement for proper topsoil management in the phase 2 remediation as it is the prerequisite for optimal revegetation after a successful close-out.30. SDN-led CSOs demanded that the ex-situ method proposed by Transcend Construction Company Ltd for the remediation of SMR lot 27 needs to be closely monitored by HYPREP to ensure strict compliance, and that biosparging should be applied to ensure optimal treatment of residual contaminants31. SDN-led CSOs observed that Thaworld Global Resources Limited, the contractor for SMT Lot 030 did not include a plan for topsoil management in their remedial action plan (RAP), and demanded that the contractor should include a plan to handle topsoil separately during excavation, treatment and backfilling. They charged HYPREP to ensure that contractors comply with this, and that failure should attract severe punishment.32. SDN-led CSOs observed that the design of remedial action for contaminated soil submitted by Thaworld Global Resources Limited, the contractor for SMT Lot 030, is generic, not detailed, and not well adapted accordingly in line with the findings (pollution levels) of the site characterization. Hence, they demanded that the plan should be detailed, informative, clear and specific to the site.33. SDN-led CSOs observed that the standard operating procedure for soil remediation processes (SOP) submitted by Thaworld Global Resources Limited, the contractor for SMT Lot 030 is generic, with sensitive details such as depth of excavation not clearly specified, and thus demanded that the section should be detailed and clear.34. SDN-led CSOs demanded that Foxtrot O & G Company Nigeria Ltd, the contractor for SMR LOT 009 should include a detailed plan for handling topsoil during their remedial action (i.e., remediation work) and that the plan should be documented in the RAP.35. SDN-led CSOs observed that the groundwater treatment design proposed by Foxtrot O & G Company Nigeria Ltd, the contractor for SMR Lot 009, is fair but requires additional technology such as pump-and-treat because of the high level of groundwater pollution (up to 183,069.3mg/L) to help to significantly reduce TPH concentration in the groundwater, making sure that the hydrocarbon-degrading microbes could effectively metabolize the remaining hydrocarbons within the specified phase 2 treatment timeframe while ex-situ methods would then be used to quickly treat groundwater pumped out from highly polluted zones.36. SDN-led CSOs observed that the remedial action proposed by Satel Construction Nig. Ltd. for the treatment of groundwater in SMR Lot 21 is insufficient, considering the extent of pollution learning from the Phase 1 groundwater remediation (for simple sites), and thus demanded that additional technology, preferably an additional combination of technologies such as soil vapour extraction (SVE), pump-and-treat methods should be added to the proposed biosparging to ensure effective groundwater treatment. They also charged HYPREP site supervisors to closely monitor the contractors to ensure compliance with the dictates of the RAP.37. SDN-led CSOs demanded that the biocells should be roofed to avoid overflooding and overflowing of the leachate, which occurred during simple site remediation and caused secondary pollution. 38. SDN-led CSOs demanded that HYPREP takes the expertise of its contractors into consideration to ensure that companies that have the requisite capacity are engaged to carry out large-scale remediation of the highly contaminated sites such as the simple medium-risk sites.39. SDN-led CSOs observed that Katech Construction Co. Ltd., the contractor for SMR Lot 018, did not include a detailed plan for handling topsoil (excavation and backfilling) in their RAP, and demanded that it should be included and documented.40. SDN-led CSOs demanded that Geokooy Environmental Services Ltd., the contractor for SMR Lot 007 should make a provision for handling topsoil separately and for ensuring it is backfilled last, and warned that topsoil should not be mixed and homogenized with soil from other strata as specified in the company's RAP.41. SDN-led CSOs warned that the chemical oxidation remediation techniques proposed by Avondale Services and Supplies Ltd, the contractor for SMR Lot 002 might result in secondary pollution by the oxidising chemical compound/radical if not properly administered, and recommended that ex-situ methods be considered instead since they are greener technologies.

title.narrative: Number of actions taken by HYPREP to progress activities of the Ogoniland clean-up in response to issues identified by the project, where there is evidence that this is as a result of project activities.

description.narrative: Records of stakeholder engagement meetings, Ogoniland and contractor records, and project documentation.

comment.narrative: Minutes and records of engagement
After several engagements with HYPREP they approved the independent monitoring of the project activities

List of relevant actions taken by HYPREP:1. As a result of our work, HYPREP invited SDN to participate at the water project kick-off meeting with contractors.2. HYPREP invited SDN to its Project Review Meeting to make inputs to improve the clean-up process.3. NOSDRA committed to taking samples from the bio-cell area to limit the possible issue of secondary contamination. 4. HYPREP invited SDN, CEHRD, and YEAC to review their communication strategy. 5. HYPREP organized a workshop to discuss the recommendation of the biannual report. This workshop also proposed the risk-based remediation close-out criteria. 6. HYPREP has included SDN and other CSOs as part of the sustainable water project working group/committee7. As a result of our work, HYPREP invited SDN to participate in their 2022 World Environment Day celebration where a collective commitment to deliver a quality clean-up of Ogoniland was collectively re-emphasized. This was held on the 6th of June 2022 at Khana LGA.8. HYPREP invited SDN to participate and contribute to their workshop on the detailed site characterization, remediation strategies and framework development for Ogoni Clean-up. This was held at Vineyard Event Centre, Woji Road, GRA Port Harcourt, from 21st -22nd July 2022.9. As a result of our continuous recommendation to HYPREP for a sustainable clean-up exercise, HYPREP invited SDN to participate and contribute to their anti-bunkering/re-pollution sensitization/seminar and award of certificates to community remediation workers trained in basic remediation techniques and HSE at Tai LG Secretariat on the 11th of August.10. As a result of our recommendation to HYPREP to hasten the delivery of potable water provision and livelihood components of the clean-up exercise, HYPREP asked SDN to participate in the Ogoni power project sensitization workshop. This was held on the 5th of September 2022 at Gbere-Saaro Hall, Gokana LGA11. HYPREP invited SDN-led CSOs to a stakeholder engagement on the progress of the HYPREP remediation works. It was held on the 6th of September 2022 at the HYPREP office.12. HYPREP asked for SDN's input on the Center of Excellence for Environmental Restoration (CEER) and invited SDN to participate in the kick-off meeting for the design of the CEER which was held on the 9th of September 2022 at HYPREP office where SDN suggested that the centre should be designed to accommodate a male to female ration of 50:50. 13. HYPREP invited SDN to participate in the Ogoni Shoreline Remediation Sensitization programme which was held on the 27th of September 2022 at Gbere-Saaro Hall, Gokana LGA.14. During SDN-led stakeholders meeting in December 2022, HYPREP promised Botem community a potable water booster station as a result of our engagement.15. HYPREP resolved the lingering water station issue between K.Dere and B.Dere by promising K.Dere a separate water booster station during the SDN-led stakeholders meeting in December 2022. This has prevented age-long inter-communal conflicts between K.dere and B.dere and has helped to make water available to the two communities independently. Before now K.dere community was somewhat sidelined by HYPREP in the provision of water for refusing to use the same booster station as B.dere.16. As a result of the reports of SDN monitoring of the cleanup and published statements, 15 lots having TPH and other parameters above the threshold were all revisited: some were monitored further while some were reworked.17. As a result of SDN's engagement with HYPREP on the need to urgently address the health condition of Ogoni people in line with UNEP recommendation, HYPREP has completed the design of an ultra-modern Hospital at Tai LGA, with land secured for this purpose.18. Due to our engagement with and recommendation to HYPREP to improve the existing livelihood programs, more livelihood programs were created for youths, women, and physically challenged people on vocational, technical, and non-technical skills.202319. HYPREP have begun to take soil samples at biocell areas for 45 lots to check and monitor secondary pollution as a result of poor clean-up. This is as a result of SDN recommendations in biannual reports.20. HYPREP has developed a detailed technical contract agreement with clean-up contractors to promote effective remediation exercise. This is in response to SDN's concerns in our biannual reports over poor standard operating procedures for the exercise.21. HYPREP included detailed standard operating procedures for remediation work in the contract document for the new contractors of the simple medium-risk sites in line with SDN’s recommendation.22. HYPREP invited SDN to the kick-off of Batch 2 of the potable water projects where we addressed the contractors on the need to follow HYPREP guidelines.23. HYPREP awarded more potable water contracts in line with SDN’s recommendation for wider and quicker delivery of the emergency measures prescribed by HYPREP.24. HYPREP has considered and is currently in the process of recruiting two senior M&E officers to improve the effective implementation of their interventions for feedback and learning.25. HYPREP made a commitment to develop soil management guidelines to ensure a proper backfilling process after site remediation to prevent poor soil management by contractors and ensure quality remediation work.26. HYPREP acknowledged SDN's recommendation for technical monitoring of remediation sites and agreed to ensure it is implemented so as to ensure effective remediation.27. HYPREP agreed with SDN's recommendation to adopt a combination of bioremediation technologies in the Phase 2 remediation projects to ensure quicker and more effective bioremediation as an improvement on the lapses of the Phase 1 exercise.28. HYPREP has adopted milestone-based payment of contractors to ensure effective management and accountability of contractors in the remediation process.29. HYPREP made a commitment to improve their community engagement guidelines to improve community participation and satisfaction and to improve the contractor-community relationship30. In line with SDN's recommendation for improved stakeholder engagement at the community level, HYPREP conducted for the first time, a stakeholder meeting with the community leadership. 31. HYPREP has included community content in the clean-up which according to them is even beyond the local content in response to the CSOs' recommendation for a people-centred stakeholder management process. Communities were pleased with this update.32. HYPREP clarified the status of the Ogoni clean-up exercise by presenting a comprehensive update of the clean-up exercise to CSOs and communities. Community members attested that the stakeholders meeting has served as a platform where they have gained more, clearer insight into the work of HYPREP.33. HYPREP made a commitment to ensure that yet-to-be-certified simple site lots with poor revegetation will be well remediated before certification.34. In response to our monitoring findings and those of HYPREP, HYPREP reclassified three simple site lots to complex sites to enable effective remediation.35. In response to SDN findings and recommendations, HYPREP put more simple site lots on six months post-remediation monitoring to ensure contaminant levels are below threshold values before certification.36. HYPREP acknowledged the poor revegetation of of remediated lots and made a commitment to apply the best remediation technology including in-situ technologies for the SMR sites (Phase 2) to ensure effective remediation, learning from the Phase 1 remediation project.37. HYPREP made a commitment to continuously review their communication strategy to ensure effective communication of HYPREP activities in Ogoniland.HYPREP promised to address all concerns raised by the stakeholders.2024In response to SDN monitoring findings, including those from HYPREP, the following actions were taken by HYPREP:38. HYPREP included SDN-led CSOs as members of a very technical committee called the Remediation Documentation Review Committee (RDRC) to review the remediation documentation submitted by phase 2 remediation of simple medium-risk sites.39. HYPREP directed its phase 2 remediation contractors to include topsoil management plans in their remedial action plans for simple medium-risk sites.

title.narrative: The National Oil Spills Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA), legislators, and the oil and gas industry, takes action to improve the prevention and reduction of emissions from the oil and gas industry, which cause local environmental damage and contribute to global climate change.
Number and type of policy/legislative changes or commitments at the Federal-level to reduce the environmental impact of the oil and gas industry, secured as a result of project activities

description.narrative: At least 2 policy/legislative changes or commitments secured at the Federal-level o reduce the environmental impact of the oil and gas industry

comment.narrative: - The 9th House Committee on Environment made a commitment to collaborate with SDN to address lingering environmental legislation issues. To this end, they requested technical, collaborative support from SDN.- The 9th House Committee on Environment has made a commitment to use a stakeholders engagement session (if SDN could facilitate this) to get feedback on the HCDT process from host communities, and thereafter push for the amendment of the HCDT section of the PIA to reflect a fair and transparent HCDT process.- The 9th House Committee on Environment made a commitment to push for an amendment of the PIA to address the lingering environmental issues such as gas flaring so as to strategically reduce gas pollution by deploying more gas utilization options. To this end, the committee requested input from SDN on more gas utilization options to enable them to recommend the same while pushing for the amendment.- The 10th House Committee on Environment made a commitment to move a motion to halt the divestment in the oil and gas sector pending the investigation of recent divestment deals to determine whether they align with international best practices which will ensure a cleaner environment.- The 10th House Committees on Environment and Host Communities made a commitment to move a motion for the amendment of the PIA to include provisions that support a transparent divestment process with SDN providing technical support.- The 10th House Committee on Environment requested that SDN should provide the committees with more facts that show that it is more efficient to have the environmental regulation of the oil and gas sector handled by a well-funded independent government regulatory agency which is separate from the agencies regulating the actual operations in the oil and gas industry. This is in an effort to address the regulatory gaps that led to the current state of environmental degradation in the Niger Delta arising from pollution from the oil industry.- The 10th House Committee on Host Communities made a commitment to take legislative actions that will ensure the operationalization of the HCDT process is transparent including proposing relevant amendments to the HCDT section of the PIA.- The 10th House Committees on Environment and Host Communities made a commitment to recommend that the NUPRC should integrate the proposed National Principles for Responsible Oil Industry Divestment into the existing framework(s) for regulating divestments in the oil and gas sector. - SDN secured a commitment from the 10th NASS Committees on Environment and Host Communities to push for the amendment of the PIA to reflect improved divestment and HCDT processes. - The 10th House of Representatives, using the improved knowledge gained from the SDN training and engagement, halted the proposed divestments in the oil and gas sector until clean-up is carried out.- In October 2024, the House Committees on Petroleum Resources (both Upstream and Downstream), Environment, Host Communities, andGas, summoned all the companies involved in the oil industry divestment to appear before the Committee in November to explain the processes they took to carry out their respective divestments in order to equip the Committee with more information needed to direct further actions to ensure responsible oil industry divestment. SDN provided the technical input to this action.

title.narrative: Number and type of actions taken by NOSDRA and oil and gas companies to reduce oil spills, gas flares and methane emissions, or improve the clean-up of oil spills, where there is evidence this is as a result of project activities – and where possible, an estimated measure of reduction/avoided emissions as a result of this (barrels of oil spilled, volume of gas flared, volume of methane emitted)

description.narrative: At least 3 actions are taken by NOSDRA and oil and gas companies to reduce oil spills, gas flares and methane emissions, or improve the clean-up of oil spills

comment.narrative: - N0SDRA joined the Biocell sampling in phase 2 remediation as recommended during the project stakeholder engagement forums.- NOSDRA sampled bio cell area before and after remediation as recommended during the project stakeholder engagement forums.- NOSDRA committed to monitoring contractor's activities before certification- NOSDRA has demanded/requested HYPREP to share their Remediation Action Plan (RAP)- NOSDRA to include timeline for revisiting lots- NOSDRA took action by contracting and instructing the operation mobilization on the Ebuocha spill as a result of SDN's swift report of the spill >>- As a result of our advocacy engagement with NOSDRA on the need to improve on their processes, the Agency has taken over the management of the oil spill monitor and gas flare tracker to enable them to modify the tools to improve on their oversight functions of oil and gas pollution monitoring and emission reduction in the oil and gas sector.- NOSDRA, following the successful alignment of our methane tracker technology initiative with the nation’s commitment to global methane emission reduction, has approached the federal government for support, and as a result, the gas flare tracker has been selected by the federal government as a reference tool in focus for building a methane tracking tool for the nation.- NOSDRA expanded the nomination of staff members for a train-the-trainer program to include staff from all their zonal offices in the country. These staff members were trained as trainers for the agency for better management of oil spills and oil spill cleanup/remediation. - NOSDRA authorized and ordered a repeat of the remediation of 4 clean-up lots in Ogoniland as a result of the wider SDN advocacy for a cleaner Niger Delta and proper remediation of oil spills in the country.- NOSDRA invited SDN to participate and contribute to the review of their JIV form to reflect best practise in oil spill incident reporting.- NOSDRA invited SDN to make inputs to groundwater remediation technology for more effective groundwater remediation. SDN recommended quicker response and containment by IOCs to avoid the extent of groundwater pollution after oil spills.- NOSDRA informed SDN of the challenges they face with the NUPRC which is affecting their regulatory work so that SDN could include them in their advocacies with the incoming committees.- NOSDRA invited SDN to contribute to the drafting of their oiled wildlife contingency plan (OWCP)so that it will be integrated into the national oil spill contingency plan (NOSCP). This will help to address and thus reduce the impact of oil spills on wildlife including those in the Niger Delta.- NOSDRA presented the GFT to high-level stakeholders including the legislators and oil industry stakeholders ad used its data to regulate and drive reduced gas flaring in the oil and gas industry and in the Niger Delta. The GFT was adopted by the Presidency in 2023 as a national tool for quantifying gas flares in the oil and gas industry, and data from the tool will be used for regulatory purposes.- NOSDRA, building on the EPI initiative, developed additional key performance indicators such as speed of response, payments of penalties, etc for ranking companies in order of their compliance with their environmental regulatory oversights.- NOSDRA made a commitment to give awards to the best environmentally performing companies using the EPI initiative in order to encourage increased environmental performance in the sector.- Oil companies made a commitment to improve their environmental performance if they could understand clearly the framework and company-wise ranking used in the 2019 and 2020 EPIs.- The Minister of State for Environment made a commitment to work with SDN to promote mangrove protection and restoration in the Niger Delta.- NOSDRA agreed that SDN should lead fundraising for the development of the full-phase methane tracker so that it could become a live tool for driving methane emission reduction in the Nigerian oil and gas industry.- NOSDRA gave 8 awards to good environmentally performing oil industry operators to encourage improved environmental performance in the oil and gas sector.- NOSDRA gave an award to Akwa-Ibom State for being the most environmentally friendly host state for the oil and gas industry. This is an effort to encourage improved environmental consciousness, performance and operator-community relationships in the oil industry host communities in Nigeria.

comment.narrative: - The Dutch Embassy asked that research on the impact of gas on host communities be conducted to serve as a guide for controlling the impacts due to the expected increase in gas investments as a result of the Russia-Ukraine war. This is what led to the research in Obrikom community in ONELGA, Rivers State. - As a result of SDN briefings, UNEP was engaged by the international community (Niger Delta contact group) following their threat to end their technical support to HYPREP. Consequently, the issues were addressed. The engagement contributed to UNEP's continued stay/support to HYPREP in the ongoing oil spill cleanup in Ogoniland.In response to the findings from the gas impact research above, Agip is being engaged to take corrective and mitigative actions on the environmental and social impacts of oil and gas exploitation and to peacefully resolve the discord between them and the host communities. They have opened the door to further engagements on this.- Because of our extensive work in the Niger Delta, the Centre for Research on Multinational Corporations (SOMO) approached SDN and requested us to support them in their research and investigations on divestment and decommissioning issues in the Niger Delta. We assisted them to move around some communities in the Niger Delta where there are divestment and decommissioning issues and also helped them to organise meetings with communities, CSOs and government agencies to aid their research. This research brought about the key recommendations that they (SOMO) published globally and submitted to the office of the UN Secretary-General for responsible oil industry divestment.
